beats.text: Five poems that lodge in your memory and never quite leave.
One. 'If—' by Kipling. A father's quiet instructions for becoming unshakeable.
Two. 'Invictus' by Henley. 'I am the master of my fate, I am the captain of my soul.'
Three. 'Ozymandias' by Shelley. A shattered statue in the sand, mocking every empire's pride.
Four. 'The Road Not Taken' by Frost. The quiet weight of the choices that shape a life.
Five. 'Death Be Not Proud' by Donne. A fearless, furious staring-down of death itself.
A great poem says in ten lines what prose needs ten pages for. Read one aloud tonight.
